findings.title: Unchecked property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` will set `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array `[]` (which many callers now pass when no destination calendar is configured). Line 119 then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining (`?.`), which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever an event's location is Google Meet (`MeetLocationType`) and the user has no destination calendar.

findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition when setting organization slug
findings.body: Line 151 was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts the intended logic: when team billing is enabled, the slug is only supposed to be stored as `requestedSlug` in metadata until payment/verification completes, and when team billing is disabled (self-hosted), `slug` should be set directly on the organization at creation time. With this change, self-hosted instances no longer get `slug` set on created organizations, while billed instances get `slug` set immediately before billing completes.

findings.title: Fallback lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent compares against falsy externalCalendarId
findings.body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`), comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` will never match a valid calendar `externalId` and will always evaluate to `undefined`.

findings.title: Google Meet patch call can receive undefined calendarId instead of falling back to "primary"
findings.body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (whereas previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, patching the Google Meet hangout link into the event description will fail because `calendarId` is missing.

findings.title: Co-host destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set (lines 1063-1067). On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null`, so if the primary organizer has not set a destinationCalendar, all collective co-hosts' `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and calendar events are not created in their destination calendars.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first destinationCalendar instead of matching the current credential
findings.body: In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (line 128), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (line 156), the target calendar is chosen via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. In a collective event with multiple hosts, `event.destinationCalendar` contains entries for all hosts, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` invokes `createEvent` for each host's credential. Using `event.destinationCalendar[0]` means a co-host using Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV will attempt to create the event using the first host's `externalId` (which belongs to a different user/account) instead of finding the `DestinationCalendar` entry matching the credential being used.
